mainTopic: Gentile wine items, fish brine, the cheese of בית אונייקי, and the dung of forbidden animals
overview: This amud first finishes a list of gentile wine items, such as canteens, grape pits and dark jugs, that become permitted after twelve months. Next the גמרא discusses מורייס, a fish brine that gentiles sometimes mixed with wine. Brine made by a professional is permitted, but only for the first two batches, because after that wine is added to make up for the missing fish oil. A story about רבי אבא guarding a boat of brine in עכו shows that the worry exists only where adding wine makes money. Then ריש לקיש explains that the cheese of בית אונייקי is forbidden because most calves there are slaughtered for עבודה זרה. The גמרא works out why 'most' is needed: a minority of a minority does not worry even רבי מאיר. ריש לקיש then defends his ruling against a charge that he contradicts himself. Finally, רב rules that קידושין with the dung of a שור הנסקל works, but with the dung of idolatrous calves it does not. The גמרא supports this with logic and with a פסוק, and רבא begins to show that the משנה hints at both rulings, a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Arab canteens are permitted after twelve months
steps.stepSummary: Canteens belonging to Arabs, which held gentile wine, become permitted after twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Canteens of Arabs: after twelve months of the year, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a list of gentile wine vessels that become permitted after a full year without use. This item is canteens used by Arabs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine soaked into a vessel is a problem of יין נסך. Once twelve months pass, the absorbed wine is treated as dried out and gone, so the vessel may be used.

phrases.english: Canteens belonging to Arabs,
after twelve months of the year, they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבַטָּא דְּטַיָּיעֵי, בָּתַר תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (before this section) of gentile wine vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arab canteens used for wine are permitted after twelve months.

steps.title: Aramean grape pits are permitted after twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא adds Aramean grape pits to the twelve-month list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: These grape pits of the Arameans are permitted after twelve months of the year.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds one more item to the same list. Aramean grape pits also become permitted after twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule stays the same, and only the item changes. Each אמורא tells us that the twelve-month rule also covers another kind of wine-related object.

keyTerms.meaning: Grape pits (left over from pressing wine)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, said:
These grape pits of the Arameans,
after twelve months of the year, they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another item to the twelve-month list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Aramean grape pits are permitted after twelve months.

steps.title: Brown and black jugs are permitted after twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא adds brown and black jugs to the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said: These brown and black jugs are permitted after twelve months of the year.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives the last item in the list: brown and black jugs. They are also permitted after a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the list of twelve-month rulings. The vessels are still in the category of gentile wine vessels. The twelve months are simply how they become usable again.
steps.whatToRemember: Many kinds of gentile wine items (canteens, grape pits, brown and black jugs) become permitted after twelve months of non-use.

phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said:
These brown and black jugs,
after twelve months of the year, they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item in the twelve-month list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brown and black jugs are permitted after twelve months.

steps.title: Fish brine made by a professional is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's word מורייס and brings a ברייתא: מורייס made by a professional is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'and the fish brine.' The רבנן taught: Fish brine made by a professional is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new item in the משנה, מורייס, which the משנה forbids. A ברייתא limits that rule: if a professional made it, it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids gentile מורייס because wine was sometimes mixed into it. The ברייתא says a professional brine-maker does not add wine, so his product has no יין נסך concern.

keyTerms.meaning: Fish brine, a salty liquid from fish, sometimes mixed with wine

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the משנה. The משנה forbids מורייס in general. The ברייתא only permits it when a professional made it.

phrases.english: And the fish brine.
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's own words, quoted from its list of forbidden gentile foods.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Fish brine made by a professional is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מורייס prepared by a professional is permitted.

steps.title: A professional's חילק is also permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן גמליאל, quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, says חילק made by a professional is also permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: חילק made by a professional is also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא adds to the ברייתא's leniency. חילק, a different fish product listed in the משנה, is also permitted when a professional makes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אף ('also') shows he applies the same reasoning to a second item. A professional does not mix in wine, so חילק made by one is permitted too.

keyTerms.meaning: A small fish or fish product listed in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Gamliel says
in the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel:
Also, chilak made by a professional is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the professional leniency to חילק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חילק prepared by a professional is permitted.

steps.title: Only the first two batches are permitted
steps.stepSummary: אבימי teaches the ברייתא and explains that only the first and second batches of a professional's מורייס are permitted, but the third is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי son of רבי אבהו taught: Fish brine made by a professional is permitted. He taught it and he explained it: the first and second time it is permitted, the third time it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אבימי repeats the ברייתא and then adds his own limit on it. Brine pressed from the same fish is permitted the first and second time, but not the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency for a professional is now narrower. Even a professional's brine is forbidden from the third batch on. The reason is given in the next steps.

keyTerms.term: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He taught it, and he himself explained it

phrases.english: Avimi, son of Rabbi Abbahu, taught:
Fish brine made by a professional is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: He taught it, and he also explained it:
The first and second time, it is permitted,
the third time, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ברייתא's leniency from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A professional's מורייס is permitted only for the first two batches. The third is forbidden.

steps.title: Why is the third batch different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אבימי's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the first two batches are permitted and the third is not. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a professional does not add wine, it is not clear why the batch number should matter. The question asks what changes by the third batch.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the third batch of a professional's מורייס is forbidden while the first two are permitted.

steps.title: Less fish oil means wine may be added
steps.stepSummary: In the first two batches the fish oil is plentiful, so no wine is needed. Later batches have wine added.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first and second time, since their oil is plentiful, there is no need to put wine in them. From then on, they put wine in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers. The early batches have plenty of fish oil and need no wine, but later batches are weaker, so wine is mixed in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a professional adds wine once the fish's oil runs low. So his reliability only holds while there is no reason to add wine, which is the first two batches.
steps.whatToRemember: A professional's מורייס is trusted only while there is no reason to add wine. Once the fish oil runs low (from the third batch on), wine is added and the brine is forbidden.

phrases.english: The first and second time, since their oil is plentiful,
there is no need to put wine in them;
from here on, they put wine in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Early batches have enough fish oil and need no wine. Later batches are made up with wine.

steps.title: רבי אבא places guards on a boat of fish brine
steps.stepSummary: A boat of מורייס arrived at the port of עכו, and רבי אבא placed guards with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain boat of fish brine came to the port of עכו. רבי אבא of עכו placed guards with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבי אבא put guards on a shipment of fish brine in עכו so no wine would be added, and this sets up רבא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guards were there to stop wine from being mixed into the brine. This shows the concern about wine in מורייס was taken seriously in practice.

phrases.english: A certain boat of fish brine
that came to the port of Akko,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתֵיב רַבִּי אַבָּא דְּמִן עַכּוֹ נָטוֹרֵי בַּהֲדַהּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba of Akko placed guards with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical story about guarding מורייס from wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבא guarded the incoming מורייס so wine would not be mixed in.

steps.title: Who guarded it until now?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges: if guarding is needed, who guarded the brine on its whole trip until now?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Until now, who guarded it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא questions why guards are needed now. Nobody watched the brine before it arrived, so guarding it only now seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question looks like a request for information, but it is really a challenge. If the brine could have been mixed with wine on the way, guarding it at the port does not help. If it couldn't have been, the guards are not needed.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Until now, who guarded it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: עַד הָאִידָּנָא מַאן נַטְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבא's action in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's placing guards on the brine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The brine was not watched on its journey, so guarding it only at arrival seems useless.

steps.title: Before now, wine was too expensive to add
steps.stepSummary: Until now there was nothing to worry about, because where the brine came from, wine cost four times as much as fish brine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Until now, what should we worry about? If it is because they mix wine into it, a measure of fish brine costs one luma, while a measure of wine costs four luma.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers that there was no worry until now. Wine cost four times more than brine where it was made, so nobody would mix wine in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern depends on price. Nobody adds an expensive liquid to stretch a cheap one. Before arrival the concern did not apply, so guards were only needed once the brine reached עכו.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure (a vessel of fixed size)

steps.whatToRemember: The worry that wine is mixed into מורייס only applies where adding wine makes money. When wine is more expensive than the brine, there is no concern.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a rabbinic suspicion like this one is based on what people actually do. Where nobody gains from mixing in wine, the suspicion does not apply.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אבא answering רבא.

phrases.english: Until now, what should we worry about?
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'who' in round brackets; the corrected wording in square brackets says 'what', so read it that way.

phrases.english: If it is because they mix wine into it,
a measure of fish brine sells for one luma,
a measure of wine sells for four luma.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד הָאִידָּנָא (לְמַאן) [לְמַאי] נֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between the situations based on price: the concern did not exist before arrival.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The brine needed guarding on its whole journey, so guarding only at the port makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where it came from, wine was more expensive than brine, so there was no concern until it reached עכו.

steps.title: Maybe the boat passed through צור
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges the previous answer: maybe the brine came by way of צור, where wine is cheap, so wine may have been mixed in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: Maybe they came by way of צור, where wine is cheap?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה questions the answer we just heard, that there was nothing to worry about on the trip. He suggests the boat may have passed through a place where wine was cheap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 we learned there was no worry because where the brine came from, wine was expensive. רבי ירמיה points out that if the boat stopped in צור, where wine is cheap, someone could have added wine there. So the brine might need guarding after all.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
Perhaps they came by way of Tyre,
where wine is cheap?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא: דִּלְמָא אַיְּידֵי דְּצוֹר אֲתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 11 that there was no need to guard the brine during the trip.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the brine was never at risk of having wine added on its journey.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if wine was expensive at the source, the boat may have passed through צור, where wine is cheap, and wine could have been added there.

steps.title: The צור route was blocked
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the route through צור had obstacles and melted snow, so the boat did not go that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, there are obstacles and melted snow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רבי ירמיה's challenge. The boat could not have come through צור because that route was too hard to travel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if the boat actually passed through צור. רבי זירא says that route was full of obstacles and melted snow, so boats did not use it. That means the brine never passed through a cheap-wine area, and the answer from Step 11 stands.

phrases.english: He said to him: There,
there are obstacles and melted snow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם עִיקּוּלֵי וּפָשׁוֹרֵי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer: the route in question was not actually used.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The boat might have passed through צור, where wine is cheap.
steps.terutzMaskana: The route through צור was blocked by obstacles and slush, so the boat did not pass there, and there was no worry.

steps.title: Why the cheese of בית אונייקי is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about גבינת בית אונייקי, and ריש לקיש explains it is forbidden because most calves in that city are slaughtered for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned the cheese of בית אונייקי. ריש לקיש said: Why did they forbid this cheese? Because most of the calves in that city are slaughtered for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new item from the משנה: the cheese of בית אונייקי. ריש לקיש gives the reason it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cheese was made using material from a calf's stomach. In this city most calves were slaughtered for עבודה זרה, so the cheese made with them is forbidden. Note that ריש לקיש says 'most' calves; the next step will ask why he needed a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Cheese from the place called בית אונייקי

phrases.english: And the cheese of Beit Unyaki.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, which lists it among forbidden items.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
For what reason did they forbid the cheese of Unyaki?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרוֹב עֲגָלִים שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ עִיר
phrases.english: Because most of the calves of that city
are slaughtered for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְבִינַת בֵּית אוּנְיָיקֵי. אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, moving away from the fish brine discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cheese of בית אונייקי is forbidden because most calves in that city are slaughtered for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Why mention a majority if a minority is enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש needed 'most' calves, since רבי מאיר worries even about a minority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically 'most calves'? Even a minority should be enough, since רבי מאיר worries about a minority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's wording. If רבי מאיר forbids things even because of a minority, why did ריש לקיש need to say that most calves were slaughtered for עבודה זרה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is known to be strict and worry about a מיעוט, a minority. So the cheese should be forbidden even if only some calves were used for עבודה זרה. That makes the word 'most' look unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? Why mention this detail?

phrases.english: Why specifically most calves?
Even a minority would also be enough,
since Rabbi Meir is concerned about a minority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word 'most' in ריש לקיש's explanation in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's statement that the reason is 'most calves.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר worries even about a minority, so a majority should not be needed to forbid the cheese.

steps.title: A majority of calves is a minority of all animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: if most calves are slaughtered for עבודה זרה, that is still only a minority of all animals, and רבי מאיר worries about such a minority.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'most' calves, then there is a minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. A majority of calves is needed so that, out of all the animals used for cheese, there is at least a real minority to worry about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calves are only one kind of animal used for cheese, so even most of the calves add up to just a minority of all the animals. רבי מאיר worries about a minority, so the cheese is forbidden. The next step shows why less than that would not be enough.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'minority' here is not a minority of calves. It is a minority of all the animals used for cheese, made up of the majority of the calves.

phrases.english: If you say a majority, then there is a minority.
phrases.notes: He means: most calves still counts as a minority of all the animals, which רבי מאיר worries about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the detail is needed: a majority of one group is only a minority of the whole.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי מאיר worries about any minority, 'most calves' seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: A majority of calves is needed to create a real minority among all animals, which רבי מאיר does worry about.

steps.title: A minority of calves is a minority of a minority
steps.stepSummary: If only a minority of calves were slaughtered for עבודה זרה, that would be a 'minority of a minority,' which even רבי מאיר does not worry about.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say a minority: since most calves are not slaughtered for עבודה זרה, and the other animals are also not slaughtered for עבודה זרה, it would be a minority of a minority, and רבי מאיר does not worry about a minority of a minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It shows why a minority of calves would not be enough to forbid the cheese, even for רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only some calves were used for עבודה זרה, there are two layers of permitted animals: most calves are fine, and all the other animals are fine. That leaves only a 'minority of a minority,' which רבי מאיר does not worry about. This is why ריש לקיש had to say 'most calves.'

keyTerms.meaning: A minority of a minority, a very small part

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר worries about a מיעוט, but not about a מיעוטא דמיעוטא. That is why ריש לקיש says most calves of בית אונייקי were slaughtered for עבודה זרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step sets a limit on רבי מאיר's strictness: he worries about a minority, but not about a minority within a minority.

phrases.english: But if you say a minority,
since there is a majority of calves
that are not slaughtered for idol worship,
and there are also the other animals
that are not slaughtered for idol worship —
it would be a minority of a minority,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִיעוּטָא דְּמִיעוּטָא לָא חָיֵישׁ רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Meir is not concerned about a minority of a minority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 16 by showing why a minority of calves would not be enough.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Sets a limit on the rule: a minority counts, but a minority of a minority does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even a minority of calves should be enough for רבי מאיר to forbid the cheese.
steps.terutzMaskana: A minority of calves is only a minority of a minority, which רבי מאיר ignores, so 'most calves' is needed.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בר אליקים challenges ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר אליקים asks ריש לקיש why slaughtering for עבודה זרה should matter, since ריש לקיש himself permits such an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בר אליקים said to ריש לקיש: Even if the calves are slaughtered for idol worship, so what? Aren't you the one who permits such animals?
steps.whatsHappening: A new חכם, רבי שמעון בר אליקים, attacks ריש לקיש's explanation of the cheese of בית אונייקי. He says ריש לקיש is contradicting himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the cheese is forbidden because the calves are slaughtered for עבודה זרה. רבי שמעון בר אליקים says ריש לקיש himself rules elsewhere that slaughtering with idolatrous intent does not forbid the animal. The source for that ruling comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: So what? What difference does it make?
But aren't you the one... (pointing out a contradiction)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אֶלְיָקִים
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon bar Elyakim said
to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
When they are slaughtered for idol worship,
what of it?
But you are the one who permits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to ריש לקיש's reason from step 14, after the רוב/מיעוט discussion ends.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the cheese is forbidden because the calves are slaughtered for עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש elsewhere rules that slaughtering with idolatrous intent leaves the animal permitted. So it seems he contradicts himself.

steps.title: The source: רבי יוחנן forbids an animal slaughtered with intent for a later idolatrous act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a dispute. Someone slaughters an animal planning to sprinkle its blood or burn its fat for עבודה זרה. רבי יוחנן forbids the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: If someone slaughters an animal in order to sprinkle its blood or burn its fat for idol worship, רבי יוחנן says it is forbidden. He holds that intent during one act of service can affect another act. He also holds that we learn the rules outside the מקדש from the rules inside the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing the source that shows ריש לקיש permits such an animal. First it gives רבי יוחנן's opposite view, setting up ריש לקיש's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a slaughter done while planning a later act of worship, like the blood or the fat. רבי יוחנן says this intent forbids the animal. In the מקדש, a wrong intention during שחיטה about a later act like sprinkling ruins a קרבן, and רבי יוחנן applies that same logic to עבודה זרה outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent during one act of service can affect another act
We learn the rules outside the מקדש from the rules inside it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people here. רבי יוחנן is the one who forbids. The contradiction is with ריש לקיש's view, which comes next.

phrases.english: As it was stated:
One who slaughters the animal
in order to sprinkle its blood for idol worship,
or to burn its fat for idol worship:
Rabbi Yochanan says: it is forbidden,
for he holds that one can intend from one act of service to another,
phrases.notes: He means that a thought during the slaughter, about a later act like the blood, still counts.

phrases.english: and we learn outside from inside.
phrases.notes: 'Inside' is the מקדש with its קרבנות; 'outside' is slaughtering for עבודה זרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the challenge in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: an animal slaughtered with intent to offer its blood or fat to עבודה זרה is forbidden. Intent can carry from one act of service to another, and outside is learned from inside.

steps.title: ריש לקיש permits the animal, so he seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that such an animal is permitted. This seems to contradict his reason for forbidding the cheese of בית אונייקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש says: it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the source. ריש לקיש permits the animal, which proves רבי שמעון בר אליקים's point from step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If slaughtering with idolatrous intent does not forbid an animal, then calves slaughtered for עבודה זרה should be permitted. Then their stomachs, used to make the cheese, should not cause a problem either. So ריש לקיש's reason for forbidding the cheese seems to fall apart.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מוּתֶּרֶת!
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: it is permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מוּתֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted dispute and shows the contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That ריש לקיש contradicts himself by forbidding the cheese because of slaughter for עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's own ruling permitting an animal slaughtered to offer its blood or fat to עבודה זרה

steps.title: ריש לקיש: in בית אונייקי the slaughter itself is the act of worship
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the people of בית אונייקי worship the idol through the slaughter itself. That is different from planning a later act with the blood or fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: May your fortune be raised up! I am talking about a case where the person says he is worshipping the idol by completing the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge warmly. He shows that the two cases are different, so he does not contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש permits the animal only when the idolatrous intent is about a later act, like sprinkling the blood or burning the fat. In בית אונייקי the slaughter itself is the worship. So the animal becomes forbidden right away, and the cheese made from it is forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: May your fortune be raised up (a warm blessing)
In a case where he says
At the completion of the slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש separates two cases. If the slaughter itself is the worship, the animal is forbidden. If the slaughter only aims at a later act, like the blood or fat, he permits it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows how ריש לקיש's two rulings fit together. It keeps his explanation of the cheese of בית אונייקי from step 14.

phrases.english: He said to him: may your fortune be raised up,
phrases.notes: This is a friendly blessing, a bit like saying 'great question, thank you!'

phrases.english: the case is where he says:
by completing the slaughter he is worshipping it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 18 through 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא): the slaughter itself is the worship, versus intent for a later act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calves slaughtered for עבודה זרה are just like an animal slaughtered to offer its blood or fat, which ריש לקיש permits.
steps.terutzMaskana: In בית אונייקי the slaughter itself is the act of worship, so the animal is forbidden at once. ריש לקיש's permission applies only to intent for a later act.

steps.title: רב's ruling on betrothing with the dung of a stoned ox or of idolatrous calves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about רבי ישמעאל's questions and brings רב's ruling. קידושין with the dung of a שור הנסקל works, but with the dung of calves of עבודה זרה it does not. The גמרא says it can support this with logic or with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי יהודה said: רבי ישמעאל asked.' רב אחדבוי said in the name of רב: If a man betroths a woman with the dung of an ox that is to be stoned, she is betrothed. If he uses the dung of calves of עבודה זרה, she is not betrothed. You can explain this with logic, or you can explain it from a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה and attaches to it a new ruling of רב about the dung of two kinds of forbidden animals. It ends by announcing two ways to back up the ruling, which the next steps will explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a שור הנסקל and calves of עבודה זרה are forbidden for benefit. רב says the ban stops at the ox's body, so its dung is still usable and has value, while the ban on idolatrous calves reaches even their dung. Since קידושין needs something of value you may benefit from, the first works and the second does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Dung (the waste inside or coming out of an animal)
An ox sentenced to stoning for killing a person; it is forbidden for benefit
One who betroths a woman (does קידושין)
Calves used as offerings for idol worship
'If you want, say...': introduces one of two possible explanations

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. With the stoned ox the dung is ALLOWED, so the קידושין works. With the idolatrous calves the dung is FORBIDDEN, so it does not.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: שָׁאַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: Rabbi Yishmael asked.
Rav Aḥadevoi said that Rav said:
One who betroths a woman with the dung of an ox that is to be stoned
she is betrothed;
with the dung of calves of idol worship
she is not betrothed.
If you want, say a logical reason,
and if you want, say a verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בית אונייקי discussion and returns to the next line of the משנה, adding רב's related ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין with the dung of a שור הנסקל is valid. קידושין with the dung of calves of עבודה זרה is not valid.

steps.title: The logical reason: the idol worshipper values the animal's bulk
steps.stepSummary: The idol worshipper is happy that the calf looks big, and the dung inside adds to that bulk, so the dung is part of the offering. The owner of a stoned ox gains nothing from its bulk.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, give a logical reason. With calves for עבודה זרה, the worshipper is pleased with the animal's bulk. But with an ox that is to be stoned, the owner is not pleased with its bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first support for רב's ruling: a common-sense reason why the dung of idolatrous calves is forbidden but the dung of a stoned ox is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bigger animal makes a more impressive offering, so the worshipper is glad about everything that makes the calf large, the dung included. That makes the dung part of what was offered, so it shares the ban. Nobody cares how big a stoned ox is, so its dung never becomes part of the forbidden thing.

keyTerms.meaning: He is pleased with it / it suits him

phrases.english: If you want, say a logical reason:
regarding calves of idol worship,
he is pleased with its bulk,
but regarding an ox that is to be stoned,
he is not pleased with its bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first of the two supports announced at the end of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב's distinction between the dung of a שור הנסקל and the dung of idolatrous calves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: the worshipper values the animal's bulk, so the dung counts as part of the offering. The owner of a stoned ox has no such interest.

steps.title: The verse-based source: 'nothing shall cling' versus 'its flesh'
steps.stepSummary: For עבודה זרה the תורה says 'nothing' may stick to your hand, which includes the dung. For the stoned ox it only says 'its flesh' may not be eaten, so its dung is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, bring a פסוק. It is written here, about עבודה זרה: 'Nothing shall cling to your hand.' And it is written there, about the ox: 'The ox shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten.' Its flesh is forbidden, but its dung is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second support for רב's ruling by comparing the wording of two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מאומה' (anything at all) in the עבודה זרה פסוק makes the ban total, reaching even the dung. The ox פסוק names only 'בשרו' (its flesh), which limits the ban to the body itself and leaves the dung permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is written here... and it is written there': sets two פסוקים side by side to compare them
'But this...': draws an inference from what the פסוק leaves out

phrases.english: If you want, say a verse:
It is written here:
"Nothing shall cling to your hand,"
and it is written there:
"The ox shall surely be stoned
and its flesh shall not be eaten,"
its flesh is forbidden,
but its dung is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second, verse-based support as another way to back up רב's ruling, alongside the logic of step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רב's distinction between the two kinds of dung.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 13:18 ('מאומה' = everything) compared with שמות 21:28 ('בשרו' = only its flesh).
steps.whatToRemember: עבודה זרה is forbidden 'מאומה', down to everything, even the dung. The stoned ox is forbidden only in 'בשרו', its flesh, so its dung is permitted.

steps.title: רבא: both rulings are hinted in the משנה's back-and-forth
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both of רב's rulings can be learned from the משנה. He points to רבי יהושע's reason for banning non-Jewish cheese (curdled in the stomach of a נבילה) and רבי ישמעאל's reply about the stomach of an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We learned both of these rulings in the משנה. We see this from the fact that רבי יהושע told him the cheese is forbidden because they curdle it in the stomach of a נבילה, and רבי ישמעאל answered him: Isn't the stomach of an עולה more severe than the stomach of a נבילה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to show that רב's two rulings are already hidden in the משנה's exchange between רבי יהושע and רבי ישמעאל. Here he sets up the quotes his proof is built on. The explanation of how they prove רב's rulings continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of needing the סברא or the פסוק, רבא says the משנה itself teaches these rulings. He focuses on a stomach, which is the inside part of an animal, much like dung. He sets up the two sides: a נבילה stomach in רבי יהושע's reason, and an עולה stomach in רבי ישמעאל's reply.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We learned both of them': both rulings are found in a משנה
They curdle (make milk set into cheese)
Stomach (here, the stomach used to curdle cheese)
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
A burnt-offering, which belongs to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rava said: We learned both of them,
phrases.notes: 'Both' means רב's two rulings: the stoned ox's dung and the idolatrous calves' dung.

phrases.english: from the fact that he said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהושע speaking to רבי ישמעאל in the משנה.

phrases.english: because they curdle it in the stomach of an animal carcass,
and he answers him back:
But isn't the stomach of a burnt-offering
more severe than the stomach of an animal carcass?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third source for רב's rulings, the משנה itself, in addition to the סברא and the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: Both of רב's rulings about the dung of a שור הנסקל and of idolatrous calves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's exchange: רבי יהושע's reason (curdling in a נבילה stomach) and רבי ישמעאל's reply about the stomach of an עולה.
